context:
The simulations describe small longitudinal motion in a homogeneous continuum with fixed density and a linear restoring response. Longitudinal strain, recorded as strain, and particle velocity v are both observed. The material segment is represented by a one-dimensional periodic domain with no external drive. A preparation containing several strain and velocity wavelengths is observed over time without added measurement noise. Coordinates, time and field scales are fixed.

The aim is to infer evolution laws for both fields, including the damping response that is not specified in advance. The model will then predict the strain and velocity generated by other initial profiles in the same material and small-motion regime. The inferred laws and fitted parameters are held fixed for these predictions.

units.note: Fixed scales across all trajectories; coefficients to discover are dimensionless. No physical SI calibration is claimed for these controlled prototypes.

known_relations.scope: Declared auxiliary kinematics only; no unknown evolution or constitutive law supplied.
